en.headline: New World shares plunge after HK$24.9 billion rights issue
en.dek: The developer offered 11 new shares for every existing one at a deep discount, with the Cheng family underwriting, as trading resumed on Monday.
body: New World Development shares fell sharply on Monday after the company proposed a rights issue to raise about HK$24.9 billion, according to reports from multiple outlets.

The plan offers 11 new shares for every existing share at HK$0.90 each, representing an approximately 81.5 per cent discount to the pre-suspension closing price of HK$4.87. Trading resumed after being halted on Friday, and the stock opened down nearly 46 per cent.

The controlling Cheng family, through Chow Tai Fook Enterprises, has committed to take up its full entitlement and underwrite a substantial portion of the remainder. The company said the proceeds would help reduce debt and support operations amid a weak property market.
Analysts noted the deep discount and large dilution, with theoretical dilution exceeding 75 per cent for non-participating shareholders.

zh.headline: 新世界供股集資249億元 復牌股價急挫近四成六
zh.dek: 發展商按一供十一方式以低價配售新股，鄭氏家族包銷，周一復牌後股價大幅下跌。
body: 新世界發展周一股價大幅下跌，公司日前提出供股計劃，集資約249億港元，多間傳媒報道。
計劃按每持有一股現有股份獲配十一股新股，認購價每股0.9港元，較停牌前收市價4.87港元折讓約81.5%。股價周五停牌後周一復牌，開市即跌近46%。
控股的鄭氏家族透過周大福企業承諾全數認購本身配額，並包銷大部分餘額。公司表示集資所得將用於減債及支持業務，面對疲弱樓市。
分析指折讓深及攤薄效應大，不參與供股的股東理論攤薄超過75%。
